study_title: Relative Advantage v26: Unified Consensus Operators with Directional Collinearity Suppression and Synergistic Coupling on Disorder of Consciousness Cohorts

cohorts.description: Wielek sleep EEG cohort (N=23, 11 MCS / 12 UWS)

cohorts.description: Mendeley spectral EEG cohort (N=41, 12 MCS / 29 UWS)

data_provenance.patient_isolation: Strict subject-level partition; 0 patient leakage between train/test and inner_train/inner_validation.

hypothesis_1_primary.name: Adaptive Regularized Consensus Operator (ARCO)
hypothesis_1_primary.formula: S(u, v, w) = (w_s * u^p + w_d * v^p)^(1/p) - lambda * w
hypothesis_1_primary.weight_logic: Continuous directional collinearity suppression inherited from v24/v25 core: if F_d > F_s, w_s = gamma_s*(1-act), w_d = gamma_d*(1+act); else w_s = gamma_s*(1+act), w_d = gamma_d*(1-act). act = clamp((r - theta)/(1 - theta), 0, 1). gamma = (F / F_sum)^alpha.

hypothesis_2_auxiliary.name: Bounded Synergistic Harmonic Consensus Operator (BSHCO)
hypothesis_2_auxiliary.formula: S(u, v, w) = (w_s * u^p + w_d * v^p)^(1/p) + eta * (2*u*v)/(u + v + 1e-6) - lambda * w
hypothesis_2_auxiliary.weight_logic: Harmonic interaction coupling term eta * 2uv/(u + v + 1e-6) under baseline collinearity gating (theta=0.88, alpha=0.05). Note: with epsilon=1e-6, the term is approximately degree-1 homogeneous away from zero and bounded on standard feature scales, but lacks strict global mathematical homogeneity. Negative empirical results show harmonic synergy did not improve AUC on this representation and grid, but do not prove physiological orthogonality or neural pathway dissociation.

unified_candidate.name: uhndi_v26_unified_tuned
unified_candidate.description: Unified inner-CV selection over the joint 50-configuration set (32 ARCO + 18 BSHCO with eta > 0).

tuning_and_tie_breaking.objective: Mean inner-validation AUC across 3 inner folds
complexity_priority: 1. Structural simplicity: eta=0.0 (ARCO) preferred over eta > 0.0 (BSHCO)
2. Gating conservatism: higher theta=0.88 preferred over theta=0.80
3. Curvature centrality: p=1.4 preferred over p=1.6
4. Equal base weighting: alpha=0.0 preferred over alpha=0.05
5. Minimal penalty: lambda=0.0 preferred over lambda > 0.0

primary_evaluation_metric.metric: Macro-averaged outer fold AUC across 3 cohorts (Binder, Wielek, Mendeley)
primary_evaluation_metric.aggregation: Mean of 25 outer folds per cohort, followed by unweighted macro-average across the 3 cohorts
prohibited_substitutions: Direct concatenation pooled OOF AUC across folds without explicit qualification

uncertainty_and_statistics.unit_of_analysis: Patient-level clustered paired resampling preserving cross-seed correlation (109 patients, 1,000 bootstrap draws)
uncertainty_and_statistics.reporting: Point estimate, 95% bootstrap CI, paired delta vs rmsco_v25_tuned, empirical two-tailed bootstrap p-value, and 75-fold win/tie/loss counts
uncertainty_and_statistics.aggregation_mechanics: Patient-level clustered resampling with replacement. In small test fold partitions (e.g. Wielek N=23 with ~4.6 test patients per fold), resampled folds frequently contain only one class (all 0 or all 1) or 0 subjects, making ROC AUC mathematically undefined. Such undefined folds are skipped and remaining valid folds in that draw are averaged. Only 8/1000 resamples retain all 75 folds across cohorts. This cluster score resampling distribution conditional on frozen predictions estimates sampling variability and must be distinguished from the fixed-partition 75-fold macro AUC. The empirical p=1.0 arises from discrete zero-differences (74 ties out of 75 folds) and does not prove equivalence between algorithms.
uncertainty_and_statistics.findings: arco_v26_tuned point delta vs v25 is +0.000667 with 95% CI [0.000000, 0.004011], p=1.0; uhndi_v26_unified_tuned point delta is 0.000000 with 95% CI [-0.003472, 0.003969], p=1.0. Incremental advantage is within statistical sampling uncertainty.
